understand:
The student wants a habit tracker aimed at college students — the real motivator here is the streak, so the core loop is open → tick off → see the streak grow. I should keep v1 on-device: reminders need push notifications, which is a bigger topic, so I'll list them as a "could" and explain in the scope note.

Key design decisions worth asking about: what happens when a day is missed (streak maths), whether habits are always daily (data model), and the visual tone. Complexity is beginner-friendly: one entity (Habit), three screens, local storage. React Native + Expo fits well because they'll want it on their own phone.
plan:
One data type — a Habit with an array of completed date keys. Storing dates as YYYY-MM-DD strings avoids time-zone bugs and makes streaks a simple walk backwards through days.

For a beginner, a single custom hook (useHabits) is clearer than Context + reducer: App.js calls it and passes data down. Navigation needs only two tabs and one modal, so plain state is enough — no navigation library. Build order: tokens and date helpers first (everything depends on them), then data + hook, then components, screens, and finally App.js to wire it together.
build: Writing the design tokens first so every component can import colours and spacing. The date helpers are pure functions — easy to test. In the hook, the save effect must not run before the initial load finishes, or it would overwrite saved data with an empty array. Cards get pressed feedback and accessibility labels; the add form validates the name and shows a live preview.
explain: For a beginner I'll lead with the mental model: a tree of components, data flowing down through props and actions flowing up through callbacks. The best end-to-end story is checking off a habit: tap → callback → immutable update in the hook → re-render → streak recalculated → effect saves to storage.
learn: The app exercises ten solid fundamentals, from components and props up to custom hooks, persistence and immutable updates. Quiz questions should test the subtle parts: why the save effect waits for loading, why mutation breaks re-renders, and why the streak counts from yesterday. Challenges progress from a pure-function greeting, to editing (reusing the form), to weekly targets that require changing the data model.
